title: Grand River Transit 10-year business plan presentation
subtitle: Mobility Plus, southwest Kitchener service, bus stop snow clearing, and an in-camera session on litigation and a personal matter.
overview: This special meeting centred on a presentation from Region of Waterloo staff on Grand River Transit's (GRT) 10-year business plan. The plan covers more frequent bus and train service, new routes in growing areas such as southwest Kitchener, township transit, specialized Mobility Plus service, and fare changes. Staff said they would keep seeking feedback from area municipalities through April and May 2025, with Regional Council to decide on the plan later.

Council did not vote on the plan, since it is a regional document. Members asked about Mobility Plus, southwest Kitchener timing, minibuses, bus stop snow clearing, special event travel, airport service and Cambridge. Staff said the plan has no fixed implementation schedule, so it can stay flexible, and that timing depends on future regional budgets.

Council also agreed to hold an in-camera meeting after the special meeting {{vote:m1}}. It would consider a solicitor-client privilege and potential litigation matter and a personal matter. Council then confirmed its by-laws and adjourned. Residents interested in transit can give input to the Region and GRT.

decisions.detail: Council authorized an in-camera meeting after the special meeting to consider a solicitor-client privilege and potential litigation matter and a personal matter under the Municipal Act, 2001.

debate: Councillors pressed for faster Mobility Plus access to the townships. One councillor said seniors who move into long-term care leave family in the townships who cannot drive, and the lack of door-to-door service limits family time. Staff said Mobility Plus does not currently serve the townships except in rare cases, and the plan aims to close that gap.

On southwest Kitchener, one councillor said some residents cannot walk to a bus stop today and asked for service sooner. Staff said key corridors are identified for the earlier years of the plan, but timing depends on future regional budgets. Staff also said new routes need stops, buses and operators, so there is a lag.
Asked about minibuses, staff said driver and maintenance costs dominate, so savings at scale are small. They said smaller vehicles may suit overnight service to major employers and Mobility Plus.

On bus stop snow clearing, a councillor raised snow banks that block people who use wheelchairs. Staff said the standard was tightened from 72 to 48 hours, that it was not always met in a hard winter, and that options such as grouping clearing with other work are still being considered.

Other questions covered funding and nimbleness: staff said development charges can fund stops but not operations, and that an expanded employer pass program is being explored. Councillors also raised student transit, transit to events, and Cambridge rail and LRT options.
